title: Problem 4.1
statement_text: What is the maximum fractional chromatic number of a $d$-degenerate, $K_{r}$-free graph?
context_text: A graph is $d$-degenerate if its vertices can be ordered $v_1,\dots,v_n$ so that each $v_i$ has at most $d$ neighbours among $v_1,\dots,v_{i-1}$; greedy colouring gives $\chi(G)\le d+1$, and the constructions of Zykov and Tutte show that triangle-free $d$-degenerate graphs can have chromatic number $d+1$, but with a huge number of vertices. The fractional chromatic number $\chi_f(G)$ is $1/p$ for the largest $p\in(0,1]$ such that some probability distribution on independent sets of $G$ puts every vertex in a random independent set with probability at least $p$. Harris conjectured, and Martinsson proved, that triangle-free $d$-degenerate graphs have $\chi_f(G)=O(d/\log d)$. $\log^{(b)}$ denotes the $b$-fold iterated logarithm. Johansson's bound for graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$ is $O(\Delta/\log\Delta)$ in the triangle-free case and $O_r(\Delta\log\log\Delta/\log\Delta)$ in the $K_r$-free case, so one might guess the answer $O_r(d\log\log d/\log d)$ for $K_r$-free $d$-degenerate graphs. The authors show this is false: for each $r\ge3$ and large $d$ there is a $d$-degenerate $K_r$-free graph with $\chi_f(G)\ge\Omega_r(d/\log^{(r-2)}d)$, so Harris' conjecture does not generalise in the expected way to $K_r$-free graphs for $r\ge4$. The trivial upper bound is $d+1$.
paper_title: Coloring small locally sparse degenerate graphs and related problems

title: Problem 6.1
statement_text: There are absolute constants $c,C>0$ such that every triangle-free $d$-degenerate graph $G$ on $n\le2^{cd}$ vertices satisfies $\chi(G)\le\frac{Cd}{\log(d/\log n)}$, and more generally every graph on $n\le2^{cd}$ vertices with an ordering in which every left-neighbourhood spans at most $d$ vertices and at most $d^2/f$ edges satisfies $\chi(G)\le\frac{Cd}{\min\{\log f,\log(d/\log n)\}}$. Can the upper bound $2^{cd}$ on the number of vertices assumed in these two results be weakened to $e^{\omega(d)}$ (with a corresponding improvement of the upper bound on $\chi$ when $n=e^{\omega(d)}$)? What if we additionally assume that the graph has large (constant) girth?
context_text: A graph is $d$-degenerate if its vertices can be ordered $v_1,\dots,v_n$ so that each $v_i$ has at most $d$ neighbours among $v_1,\dots,v_{i-1}$; greedy colouring gives $\chi(G)\le d+1$, and the constructions of Zykov and Tutte show that triangle-free $d$-degenerate graphs can have chromatic number $d+1$, but with a huge number of vertices. The authors prove: (main theorem) there are absolute constants $c,C>0$ such that every triangle-free $d$-degenerate graph on $n\le2^{cd}$ vertices has $\chi(G)\le\frac{Cd}{\log(d/\log n)}$; (local sparsity version) the same with $\chi(G)\le\frac{Cd}{\min\{\log f,\log(d/\log n)\}}$ for every graph on $n\le2^{cd}$ vertices with a vertex ordering in which each left-neighbourhood (set of earlier neighbours) has at most $d$ vertices and spans at most $d^2/f$ edges ($2<f<d^2$). Consequently the minimum order $f(d)$ of a triangle-free $d$-degenerate $(d+1)$-chromatic graph satisfies $e^{\Omega(d)}\le f(d)\le e^{O(d^2\log d)}$. The authors consider this the most important open problem left by the paper. Even improving the constant $c$ to a moderately large value, with an appropriate bound on $\chi$, would solve Erdős's problem on graph Ramsey numbers for all triangle-free graphs (via the trivial bound $r(G)\ge|V(G)|$ for graphs with exponentially many vertices), and perhaps for all $H$-free graphs with $H$ almost bipartite.

title: Problem 6.2
statement_text: Is the following statement true for all $\varepsilon>0$? If $G$ is a $d$-degenerate triangle-free graph with maximum degree $\Delta(G)\leq e^{d^{1-\varepsilon}}$, then we have $\chi(G)=O\left(\frac{d}{\log d}\right)$.
context_text: A graph is $d$-degenerate if its vertices can be ordered $v_1,\dots,v_n$ so that each $v_i$ has at most $d$ neighbours among $v_1,\dots,v_{i-1}$; greedy colouring gives $\chi(G)\le d+1$, and the constructions of Zykov and Tutte show that triangle-free $d$-degenerate graphs can have chromatic number $d+1$, but with a huge number of vertices. The authors prove: (main theorem) there are absolute constants $c,C>0$ such that every triangle-free $d$-degenerate graph on $n\le2^{cd}$ vertices has $\chi(G)\le\frac{Cd}{\log(d/\log n)}$; (local sparsity version) the same with $\chi(G)\le\frac{Cd}{\min\{\log f,\log(d/\log n)\}}$ for every graph on $n\le2^{cd}$ vertices with a vertex ordering in which each left-neighbourhood (set of earlier neighbours) has at most $d$ vertices and spans at most $d^2/f$ edges ($2<f<d^2$). Consequently the minimum order $f(d)$ of a triangle-free $d$-degenerate $(d+1)$-chromatic graph satisfies $e^{\Omega(d)}\le f(d)\le e^{O(d^2\log d)}$. The question asks whether the global assumption on the number of vertices can be replaced by a local one, bounding the maximum degree. Resolving it would likely require localising the random colouring process used in the paper, so that the union bound is replaced by the Lovász Local Lemma. An $H$-immersion is a graph obtained from $H$ by replacing its edges by edge-disjoint (not necessarily vertex-disjoint) paths; Lescure and Meyniel conjectured in 1988 that graphs with no $K_t$-immersion are $(t-1)$-colourable. Since by van den Heuvel and Wood every $K_t$-immersion-free graph splits into two parts inducing subgraphs of maximum degree $O(t^3)$ (and such graphs have degeneracy $O(t)$), an affirmative answer would give $\chi=O(t/\log t)$ for triangle-free graphs with no $K_t$-immersion, which would be optimal up to constants.

title: Problem 6.3
statement_text: Is it true that if the chromatic number of a $K_{r}$-free $d$-degenerate graph is $d+1$, then the graph has $e^{\Omega_{r}(d)}$ vertices?
context_text: A graph is $d$-degenerate if its vertices can be ordered $v_1,\dots,v_n$ so that each $v_i$ has at most $d$ neighbours among $v_1,\dots,v_{i-1}$; greedy colouring gives $\chi(G)\le d+1$, and the constructions of Zykov and Tutte show that triangle-free $d$-degenerate graphs can have chromatic number $d+1$, but with a huge number of vertices. The authors prove: (main theorem) there are absolute constants $c,C>0$ such that every triangle-free $d$-degenerate graph on $n\le2^{cd}$ vertices has $\chi(G)\le\frac{Cd}{\log(d/\log n)}$; (local sparsity version) the same with $\chi(G)\le\frac{Cd}{\min\{\log f,\log(d/\log n)\}}$ for every graph on $n\le2^{cd}$ vertices with a vertex ordering in which each left-neighbourhood (set of earlier neighbours) has at most $d$ vertices and spans at most $d^2/f$ edges ($2<f<d^2$). Consequently the minimum order $f(d)$ of a triangle-free $d$-degenerate $(d+1)$-chromatic graph satisfies $e^{\Omega(d)}\le f(d)\le e^{O(d^2\log d)}$. Let $f_r(d)$ be the minimum order of a $K_r$-free $d$-degenerate $(d+1)$-chromatic graph. Via a connection with on-line colouring (the on-line chromatic number $g_r(n)$ of $n$-vertex $K_r$-free graphs satisfies $g_r(n)=\Omega(n^{(r-2)/(r-1)})$), the authors get $f_r(d)\le e^{O(d^{(r-1)/(r-2)}\log d)}$ for fixed $r$. The question asks whether the exponential lower bound proved for $r=3$ also holds for every $r\ge4$; extending it would need a $K_r$-free analogue of the main colouring theorem, which seems hard with the paper's method, in particular because the fractional chromatic number bound of Martinsson (used for $r=3$) fails for $r\ge4$.

title: Problem 6.4
statement_text: Let $r\geq 4$. Is it true that the maximum fractional chromatic number of $K_{r}$-free $d$-degenerate graphs is $o_{r}(d)$?
context_text: A graph is $d$-degenerate if its vertices can be ordered $v_1,\dots,v_n$ so that each $v_i$ has at most $d$ neighbours among $v_1,\dots,v_{i-1}$; greedy colouring gives $\chi(G)\le d+1$, and the constructions of Zykov and Tutte show that triangle-free $d$-degenerate graphs can have chromatic number $d+1$, but with a huge number of vertices. The fractional chromatic number $\chi_f(G)$ is $1/p$ for the largest $p\in(0,1]$ such that some probability distribution on independent sets of $G$ puts every vertex in a random independent set with probability at least $p$. Harris conjectured, and Martinsson proved, that triangle-free $d$-degenerate graphs have $\chi_f(G)=O(d/\log d)$. $\log^{(b)}$ denotes the $b$-fold iterated logarithm. The trivial upper bound for $d$-degenerate graphs is $\chi_f(G)\le\chi(G)\le d+1$. The authors prove that for each $r\ge3$ and large $d$ there is a $d$-degenerate $K_r$-free graph with $\chi_f(G)\ge\Omega_r(d/\log^{(r-2)}d)$, which gets closer to linear in $d$ as $r$ grows, so the question is whether any asymptotic improvement over $d+1$ holds for each fixed $r\ge4$. It is closely related to the question whether $K_r$-free $d$-degenerate $(d+1)$-chromatic graphs must have $e^{\Omega_r(d)}$ vertices.
